title: Imputed Christ's righteousness: passion and obedience made ours
source_text: XXIV. Quum autem affirmant nos, per imputatam Christi justitiam, coram Deo justificari, ista formula nihil aliud significant, quam Christi passionem & obedientiam, a Deo nobis ita donari, & communicari, ut vere nostra sit, & censeri debeat, eamque sic nobis donatam esse justitiam illam, cujus merito atque intuitu solvimur a legis maledictione, quae constat, ut dictum est, perpetua a regno Dei exclusione, & abjectione in ignem aeternum.
pass_a_gloss: But when they affirm that we are justified before God by the imputed righteousness of Christ, by that formula they signify nothing else than that Christ's passion and obedience are so given and communicated to us by God that it is truly ours and ought to be counted ours, and that thus given to us it is that righteousness by whose merit and regard we are loosed from the curse of the law, which consists, as has been said, in perpetual exclusion from God's kingdom and casting into eternal fire.
pass_b_english: Imputed Christ's righteousness = his passion and obedience given as truly ours.
By its merit we are loosed from the law's curse—exclusion and eternal fire.

choices.why: Counted ours, not infused as form.
